newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japanese officials to visit N.Korea on aid mission.
newsitem.headline: Japanese officials to visit N.Korea on aid mission.

text.p: Two Japanese officials will travel to North Korea on a week-long mission from Tuesday to see how the flood-stricken communist state has been using Tokyo's humanitarian food aid.
"Two staff from our ministry will visit North Korea from today until September 17," a Foreign Ministry official said.
The officials would visit areas devastated by two years of floods and study how Japanese humanitarian aid worth $6 million was being used, the official said.
Japan agreed to offer the humanitarian aid in June in response to an appeal by the United Nations for emergency food supplies for North Korea.
The Japanese officials will exchange views with officials from international aid organisations including the World Food Programme, the U.N. food aid organisation, the official said.
But he said it was not clear whether the two officials would hold talks with North Korean officials.
Pyongyang's official media have said floods in July seriously damaged vast areas in the communist state, caused many deaths and made many people homeless.
North Korea was already widely reported to be on the brink of famine after the worst floods in a century ravaged much of the country last year, wiping out most of the rice harvest.
Japan has no diplomatic ties with communist North Korea.

Talks to normalise relations between Tokyo and Pyongyang began in 1991 but collapsed in November the following year when the North Koreans walked out after Japan demanded information about a Japanese woman alleged to have been abducted by Northern agents.
